title: Can Taste Be Owned in the Age of Generative AI?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: Taste can be recognized, taught, imitated, and commercially valuable without becoming a single ownable legal object; generative AI makes the need to separate those categories urgent.
A garment record becomes institutional evidence when material, date, maker, identifier, and rights remain attached.

01 · TASTE — What exactly is being claimed?. Separate a general sensibility from a named mark, protected work, registered design, confidential process, contractual promise, or misleading commercial representation. Precision prevents cultural grievance from being mistaken for a settled legal result.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · TRACE — What entered the process?. Keep a source log for references, licensed assets, model and tool versions, prompts, human selections, rejected outputs, edits, and final approvals. The record supports accountability without proving a legal conclusion on its own.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · TRANSFORM — Where is human judgment visible?. Describe the problem, constraints, alternatives, selection criteria, arrangement, revision, and final expressive choices. Avoid claiming that effort alone creates protection; the purpose is to preserve an accurate creative record.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · REVIEW — Which question needs counsel or permission?. Flag identifiable source works, living artists or houses named in prompts, confidential inputs, deceptive attribution, commercial marks, uncertain licenses, and jurisdiction-specific design questions for qualified review.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
